name: Personal Finance
description: Compare mortgage options, project savings growth, estimate tax obligations, and plan investments with transparent formulas and instant results.
longDescription:
Working out whether you can afford a mortgage, how fast you can pay off a loan, or what your investments might be worth in twenty years shouldn't require downloading an app or handing over your financial details. These calculators run the numbers right in your browser — amortization schedules, compound interest projections, freelance tax estimates, and more. Every formula is based on standard financial models, and the results are shown alongside the maths so you can check the working yourself. Nothing you enter leaves your device.

If you're comparing home loan options, start with the Mortgage Amortization Calculator — it generates a full payment schedule showing how much goes to principal versus interest each month, which is the clearest way to see the true cost of a loan. For longer-term planning, the Compound Interest & Wealth Growth Visualizer lets you project savings over 10, 20, or 30 years with different contribution frequencies, while the Early Retirement Visualizer adds withdrawal rate modelling so you can see when your portfolio can sustain your living expenses.

Freelancers and contractors will find the Invoice, Tax & Net Pay Calculator useful for quoting projects — it estimates quarterly tax obligations based on your income bracket and expenses, so you know your actual take-home before committing to a rate. The Car Loan Amortization & Lease Calculator handles both traditional loans and novated leases, comparing total cost of ownership across different term lengths and deposit amounts.

For home improvement decisions, the Renovation Cost Range Estimator breaks down typical Australian renovation costs by room type and scope, while the Solar Panel ROI & Savings Calculator factors in your location, electricity rates, and panel degradation to estimate payback period. Strata owners can use the Sinking Fund & Asset Life Estimator to project whether their building's capital works fund is adequately reserved.

name: Business Metrics
description: Calculate CAC, LTV, churn impact, and ad spend ROI. Evaluate SaaS health, FBA margins, and novated lease costs.
longDescription:
If you've ever stared at a spreadsheet trying to figure out your customer acquisition cost or whether that novated lease actually saves you tax, these tools are for you. They cover the core metrics founders and finance teams work with day to day — CAC, LTV, churn, CPM, SaaS ratios, FBA profit margins. The formulas are drawn from standard business and accounting practices, and each tool shows its working so you can verify the output. Everything runs locally, so sensitive revenue and cost figures stay on your machine.

SaaS founders evaluating growth health should start with the Churn, LTV & CAC Runway Calculator — it models how quickly you're burning through customer lifetime value relative to acquisition spend, and projects your runway at current churn rates. Pair it with the CPM & Digital Ad Spend ROI Calculator when evaluating whether a Facebook or Google campaign is actually profitable after factoring in impressions, click-through rates, and conversion fractions.

Amazon FBA sellers face a different challenge: the Margin & Profit Estimator accounts for referral fees, fulfilment charges, storage costs, and shipping — not just the product price — so you see the real margin before committing to inventory. For service-based businesses, the Freelance Project Scope & Budget Estimator helps you break a project into phases, allocate hours per phase, and calculate a fee that covers your actual costs plus target profit margin.

Electric vehicle owners evaluating a novated lease can use the EV or PHEV Novated Lease Calculator to compare pre-tax and post-tax costs, factoring in running costs, fringe benefits tax, and residual value. The output shows total cost of ownership over the lease term versus buying outright.

name: Maths & Numbers
description: Calculate percentages, explore Pi's digits, and discover Kaprekar's constant. Maths tools for everyday calculations and curiosity.
longDescription:
Sometimes you just need a quick percentage calculation, or you want to explore the digits of Pi, or you're curious about Kaprekar's constant. These tools handle the everyday maths that comes up at work, school, or just out of curiosity — percentage changes, number base conversions, and a few recreational maths puzzles. The calculations are straightforward and the results are instant. No accounts, no tracking, no fuss.

The Percentage Calculator handles the most common everyday scenarios: calculating a percentage of a number, finding what percent one number is of another, computing percentage increase or decrease between two values, and reverse-engineering the original number before a discount or markup. Each mode shows the formula and working so you can verify the result or use it as a learning tool.

For something more exploratory, the Pi Explorer lets you search for specific digit sequences within Pi's decimal expansion — type in your birthday or any number pattern and see where it appears. The tool displays millions of digits with a searchable index, which makes it useful for both curiosity and education about irrational numbers. The Kaprekar Constant Calculator demonstrates the iterative process where any four-digit number with at least two distinct digits eventually reaches 6174 through repeated subtraction of rearranged digits — a surprisingly elegant result in recreational mathematics.

These tools are particularly useful for students checking homework, professionals validating spreadsheet formulas, or anyone who wants to understand the arithmetic behind a calculation rather than just seeing a result.

name: Converters
description: Convert between 150+ currencies, engineering units, and everyday measurements with visible conversion factors.
longDescription:
Converting between units shouldn't feel like a chore. These converters cover length, weight, volume, temperature, pressure, energy, force, power, angle, fuel efficiency, density, and thermal properties — all using standardised conversion factors with proper attention to precision and edge cases. Whether you're converting PSI to bar for an engineering spec or Celsius to Fahrenheit for a recipe, the results are instant and the maths is visible. No server calls, no data collection, just straight conversion.

The most commonly used converters — Length, Weight, Volume, and Temperature — handle everyday tasks like recipe conversions, travel measurements, and international unit differences. The Temperature Converter is particularly useful for cooking: it converts between Celsius, Fahrenheit, and Kelvin with offset and scale adjustments handled correctly (not just a linear formula, which breaks at extreme values).

For technical work, the Pressure Converter handles PSI, bar, Pascal, atmospheres, and mmHg — critical for engineers working across metric and imperial hydraulic or pneumatic systems. The Data Storage Converter translates between bytes, kilobytes, megabytes, gigabytes, terabytes, and their binary equivalents (KiB, MiB, GiB), which matters when provisioning cloud storage or comparing drive capacities where manufacturers use decimal but operating systems use binary.

The Currency Converter pulls exchange rates and handles over 150 currencies with proper rounding rules. The Number Base Converter supports binary, octal, decimal, hexadecimal, and arbitrary bases up to base-36 — useful for developers debugging memory dumps or network packets.

All converters display the conversion factor used, so you can verify the result or apply the same factor in your own calculations.

name: Health Tools
description: Estimate BMI, BMR, calorie needs, hydration, and fertility windows. Health metrics based on WHO and clinical standards.
longDescription:
Health calculators are useful when you want a quick estimate without booking an appointment. These tools cover BMI, basal metabolic rate, calorie deficits, hydration needs, and fertility window estimates — all based on published formulas and standard medical ranges. They're not a substitute for professional advice, but they give you a starting point for understanding your own numbers. Everything stays in your browser; no health data is stored or transmitted.

The BMI Calculator uses the standard WHO formula and classifies results into underweight, normal, overweight, and obese categories using the widely adopted thresholds (18.5, 25, 30). It accepts both metric and imperial inputs, which makes it accessible regardless of which measurement system you're used to. For a more complete metabolic picture, the BMR Katch-McArdle & TDEE Calculator estimates your basal metabolic rate using the Katch-McArdle formula (which accounts for lean body mass) and then multiplies by an activity factor to give your total daily energy expenditure — useful for setting calorie targets for weight loss or muscle gain.

The Macro Nutrient & Calorie Deficit Allocator takes your TDEE and target deficit, then breaks down recommended protein, carbohydrate, and fat intake in grams and percentages. This is more practical than a single calorie number because macronutrient distribution affects satiety, energy, and body composition differently.

For hydration, the Sweat-Rate & Fluid Loss Calculator estimates how much fluid you lose during exercise based on duration, intensity, and environmental conditions — useful for endurance athletes who need to plan intake during long runs or rides. The Ovulation & Fertility Window Calendar calculates estimated fertile days based on cycle length, using the standard clinical method of counting back 14 days from the next expected period.

name: Web Tools
description: Generate colour palettes, debug JWTs, validate JSON, preview meta tags, and build redirects. Developer utilities that run in your browser.
longDescription:
Building for the web means constantly juggling formats, encoding strings, checking headers, and tweaking CSS. These tools handle the small but frequent tasks that slow you down — colour palette generation, compression analysis, password hashing, meta tag previewing, htaccess and nginx redirect building. Each tool is focused on one job and does it quickly. No sign-ups, no server round-trips, no waiting.

Front-end developers will find the Colour Palette & CSS Generator most immediately useful: enter a base colour and get complementary, analogous, and triadic palettes with ready-to-copy CSS custom properties. The CSS Flexbox & Grid Sandbox lets you prototype layouts visually before committing to code — you can test alignment, gap, and responsive behaviour in real time.

For data work, the CSV to JSON & XML Converter handles delimiter detection, header row mapping, and nested field flattening — common pain points when importing spreadsheets into APIs. The JSON Prettifier, Minifier, Fixer, and Validator form a complete JSON workflow: validate schema, fix syntax errors, format for readability, or compress for production.

The HTML Meta Tag & Open Graph Previewer generates complete meta tag blocks for Twitter Cards and Facebook Open Graph, then renders a preview of how the page will appear when shared on social platforms. The QR Code Generator & Scanner creates QR codes from URLs, text, or contact info with customizable error correction levels.

Security-focused tools include the Password Hash & Security Evaluator, which generates bcrypt, scrypt, and SHA-256 hashes and rates password strength against common attack patterns, and the Brotli & Gzip Compression Inspector, which shows the compression ratio achievable with different algorithms on your actual HTML or JavaScript.

name: Text Processing
description: Clean CSV exports, convert Markdown, deduplicate lists, and compare text diffs. Text transformations that run instantly in your browser.
longDescription:
Whether you're tidying up a CSV export, converting markdown to HTML, deduplicating a list, or just trying to figure out why your JSON won't parse, these text tools get it done. They handle whitespace cleanup, case conversion, delimiter swapping, column extraction, and a range of other string transformations. Paste your text in, pick the operation, and copy the result. Everything runs in your browser, so sensitive data never leaves your machine.

Developers working with messy data exports will find the Delimiter Swapper and Text Column Extractor most immediately useful — the first converts between CSV, TSV, and custom delimiters, while the second pulls specific columns out of a large dataset without requiring a spreadsheet app. The Duplicate Line Remover & Alphabetizer handles deduplication and sorting in a single pass, which is handy for cleaning email lists, tag arrays, or any text where duplicates have crept in.

For content work, the Markdown to HTML / Confluence Converter produces clean HTML from Markdown with proper heading hierarchy, code blocks, and table support — useful when migrating documentation between platforms. The Markdown Sanitizer & Formatter normalizes inconsistent Markdown syntax (mixed heading levels, inconsistent list markers, trailing whitespace) into a consistent style.

The Side-by-Side Visual Code Diff Checker and Text Diff & Plagiarism Compare Checker both highlight differences between two texts, but the first is optimised for code (line-level diff with syntax highlighting) while the second is designed for prose (word-level diff with similarity scoring). The Variable String Case Converter handles camelCase, snake_case, kebab-case, PascalCase, and a dozen other conventions — useful when translating between API naming styles.

name: AI Web Tools
description: Tokenise prompts, build prompt chains, test safety filters, and format structured data for AI workflows. Prompts never leave your browser.
longDescription:
Working with large language models means spending a lot of time on prompt design, token counting, and output formatting. These tools help with the practical side of that workflow — tokenising prompts, building prompt chains, checking for hallucinations, stress-testing safety filters, and formatting structured data for model input. Everything runs client-side, so your prompts and API keys never touch a server.

The Cross-Model Prompt Architect & Tokenizer is the starting point: it counts tokens using multiple tokenisation schemes (cl100k, p50k, o200k) so you can see exactly how many tokens a prompt will consume across GPT-4, Claude, and other models. This matters because token limits vary and costs are calculated per token — knowing your count before sending saves money and prevents truncation.

For more complex workflows, the Prompt Chain Builder lets you design multi-step chains where the output of one prompt becomes the input to the next. This is useful for tasks like research summarisation (search → extract → summarise → translate) or content generation (outline → draft → edit → format). Each step can specify the model and temperature, and the chain can be exported as a runnable script.

The AI Hallucination & Fact-Check Guard takes a model's output and identifies claims that should be verified against external sources, flagging statements that are likely factual (and thus checkable) versus opinion or speculation. The System Prompt Safety Stress-Tester systematically probes a system prompt for injection vulnerabilities by testing adversarial inputs that attempt to override instructions.

name: PDF Tools
description: Merge, split, compress, convert, and edit PDFs entirely in your browser. No file uploads required.
longDescription:
PDF manipulation usually means uploading your files to some random website and hoping they don't keep a copy. These tools do everything in your browser — merging, splitting, rotating, reversing pages, OCR, editing, signing, converting to and from PDF, and optimising file size. The processing happens entirely client-side using PDF.js and related libraries, so your documents never leave your device.

The most common tasks are Merge PDF and Split PDF — the first combines multiple files into a single document with drag-and-drop reordering, while the second extracts specific page ranges or splits at every N pages. Both handle large files efficiently because processing happens in memory rather than through server uploads.

For document preparation, the OCR PDF tool uses Tesseract.js to extract text from scanned documents and image-based PDFs — useful when you need to search or copy text from a paper document that was scanned to PDF. The Convert To PDF and Convert From PDF tools handle common format conversions: Word documents, images, and text files to PDF, and PDF back to images or text.

The Edit PDF tool lets you add text, annotations, and form fields directly in the browser without needing Adobe Acrobat. The Sign PDF tool supports both typed signatures and drawn signatures using your mouse or touchscreen — useful for signing contracts or approval forms digitally.

For optimisation, the Optimize & Repair PDF tool recompresses images, removes duplicate fonts, and strips metadata to reduce file size. The Secure PDF tool adds password protection with AES-256 encryption — useful before sharing sensitive documents via email.

name: Lexical Tools
description: Find anagrams, generate placeholder text, and explore word patterns. Language tools for games, writing, and education.
longDescription:
Language is more fun when you can play with it. These tools help you find anagrams, generate placeholder text, count words and characters, and explore word patterns. Whether you're stuck on a crossword, building a word game, or just curious about what words can be made from a set of letters, these tools give you instant results. No accounts, no data collection, just words.

The Anagram & Word Puzzle Finder is the flagship tool here: enter a set of letters and it finds all valid English words that can be formed from them, filtered by minimum length. It's useful for Scrabble and Words With Friends strategy, crossword solving, and word game practice. The tool uses a comprehensive dictionary and can also filter by starting letter, containing specific characters, or matching a pattern.

For content creators, the Lorem Ipsum & Dummy Text Customizer generates placeholder text in multiple styles — classic Lorem Ipsum, corporate tone, technical writing, or conversational — with control over paragraph count, sentence length, and word complexity. This is more useful than a single Lorem Ipsum generator because different design contexts need different text density and reading levels.

The Variable String Case Converter (also in Text Processing) handles case transformations for programming: camelCase, snake_case, PascalCase, kebab-case, and other conventions. The Slug Generator produces URL-safe slugs from any text, handling unicode characters, contractions, and special characters correctly.

name: Randomizers
description: Shuffle lists, flip coins, roll dice, and generate random numbers. Cryptographic randomness via the Web Crypto API.
longDescription:
Randomness is surprisingly useful — picking a winner, shuffling a playlist, generating a passphrase, simulating dice rolls, or just making a decision when you can't choose. These tools use cryptographic randomness (via the Web Crypto API) to ensure fair, unpredictable results. Whether you need a coin flip, a random number in a range, or a shuffled list, the result is instant and verifiable. Nothing is stored or transmitted.

The most frequently used tools are the Random Number Generator and the List Randomizer. The Number Generator produces integers or decimals within a specified range with configurable inclusive/exclusive bounds — useful for lotteries, sampling, simulation, or settling disputes. The List Randomizer accepts a pasted list of items (names, tasks, options) and shuffles them into a random order, which is handy for drawing raffle winners, assigning rotating responsibilities, or randomising survey response order.

The Dice Roller simulates 1-10 dice with configurable sides (d4, d6, d8, d10, d12, d20, d100) and supports advantage/disadvantage mechanics used in tabletop RPGs. The Coin Flipper produces fair heads/tails results with visual feedback — simple but useful for binary decisions.

The Alphabet Randomizer produces a shuffled alphabet, which is useful for creating substitution ciphers, generating unique colour assignments, or randomising test conditions in experimental design. The Date Randomizer generates random dates within a specified range, useful for testing date-handling code or creating sample datasets.
